html:
The voyage of the Kasato Maru, the first ship to carry Japanese emigrants to Brazil. It reached the port of Santos on 18 June 1908 with nearly 800 people on board, most of them bound for coffee farms in São Paulo state.

Brazil had abolished slavery in 1888, and coffee planters needed workers. Japan, for its part, had crowded villages and a government keen to send people abroad, while the United States and Australia were closing their doors to Asians.

Life on the farms was hard and many early migrants left them. Yet more ships followed, above all between the 1920s and 1930s, and families later bought land and grew vegetables, tea and cotton. Their descendants, now around two million, form the largest Japanese community outside Japan. See Japanese migration to Brazil. From the 1990s many moved the other way, to work in Japanese factories. The day of the landing is marked in Brazil as Japanese Immigration Day.
